sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of predicted default, and risk rises steeply as the share of the credit limit in use goes up.
The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, and risk increases with it, with most of the rise occurring between none and one or two delinquencies.
The two interact strongly: the effect of utilization is much larger for applicants with delinquencies, and the effect of delinquencies is much larger at high utilization.
Income is among the next most important features, and predicted risk decreases as income goes up.
Length of credit history is also among the next most important features, and predicted risk decreases as the history gets longer.
Debt-to-income ratio has at most a weak effect, with risk increasing as the ratio rises.
The data do not settle whether age, feature_a or feature_b matter, as their effects are too small to resolve at this sample size.
